decision: rejected; production source, artifacts, backend and identity unchanged
problem: Unique 256 KiB appends spend about 1.6 ms in receipt preparation. Receipts are first zlib-encoded, then large encoded results enter independently compressed Blob storage. A faster compatible encoder was tested before a storage representation redesign.
implementation: libdeflater/libdeflate 1.26.1 level 1 whole-buffer zlib compression writes into one initialized final allocation of raw.len bytes. Output allowance admits only strictly smaller complete receipts. InsufficientSpace copies the original bytes into the same allocation without retry or a second output allocation. Input limits, framing, legacy decoder, receipt admission, identity, validation, replay, outbox and durability remain unchanged. Adds opt-in receipt_response_encode stage.
decision_reason: All large shapes regress in the balanced initial cohort. Unique mean/CPU/P99 regress 27.8/18.9/28.8%; longer confirmation retains 22.9/15.5/77.7% regressions. Encoding observer and release-linked microprobe reproduce the cost. No release based on favorable small/read/tail/memory rows.
alternatives: Do not infer local performance from upstream descriptions; measure the actual bundled release encoder.
Compressor context caching would retain per-worker state: isolated reuse changes CPU by less than 2% in all three shapes and does not fix this regression.
Lower level zero via fastest() performs no compression and failed existing compressed/corruption checks; explicit level one restores all checks.

Raw receipts are already supported by the old decoder and fit current equal 4 MiB decoded/stored bounds. Letting Blob own the sole compression layer is a distinct future experiment, not validated or installed here.

default_off_writes.scope: Strict native production SDK on disposable local xfs. Timed latency excludes content generation; timed process CPU and phase wall include content generation. RSS is cumulative process high-water across shapes, not per-case native heap. Per-leg P99 has 200 samples and cannot certify tail dominance. Fresh processes, shared host; no performance credit for compile-overlapped driver validation.

longer_confirmation.purpose: Longer confirmation justified by 200-sample P99 regressions in initial cohort. Separate fresh processes; original adverse rows retained. No compile overlap.

resources.context_lifecycle: One C compressor allocation per compressed response, freed by binding Drop; no pool or cache. This does not imply libc returns freed resident pages immediately. Net comparison to old miniz workspace was not measured.

next_root_action.evidence: Both roles have >200 ms outliers dominated by about 186–221 ms mutex_wait, while embedded queue wait is only about 8–10 us. This redirects tail work from dispatch queue and receipt codec to shared authority holders. Default-off confirmation independently records 214–260 ms maxima on all four baseline legs and 215–230 ms on all four candidate legs; these spikes are not limited to profiling runs.
next_root_action.known_exclusion: daemon::run_rotation_driver drops its authority guard before rotation_prefix_encode. Aggregate prefix-encoding time does not prove it held the mutex.
next_root_action.priority: Add bounded attribution of rotation prepare/install, pack prepare/install, overlay capture/publish and other maintenance holds; identify the holder responsible for observed waits before moving additional work outside authority.
next_root_action.secondary_mean_cost_hypothesis: Test a single Blob compression layer for new large raw receipts, preserving exact legacy zlib replay and frozen byte bounds. No result is claimed for that unimplemented design.

limits: Disposable local xfs authorities and strict native production SDK. No new SQLite comparison, universal dominance or active-conversation certification.
Initial P99 has 200 writes/leg; confirmation 2000 small or 1000 large writes/leg. Quantiles are averaged per leg, not pooled. Raw per-request timing retained.
Latency excludes generation; CPU and phase wall include generation; read-control CPU includes exact checks. Initial RSS is cumulative across shapes; later cases use fresh processes.
Profile runs and microprobes excluded from production-off timing. Dispatch profiles exclude final response validation, reply and SDK work; wall stages are not CPU samples.

Slow-sample observer retains the 32 largest dispatches, not necessarily the largest client latencies. Request sequence is matched exactly. Counter totals cannot uniquely identify the competing mutex holder.
Shared-host activity may affect tails. The observed encoder slowdown is independently reproduced; no claim that all P99 regression is caused by the new encoder.

microprobe_scope: Separate release-linked C program with synthetic 262144-byte repetitive, 90-character random and repeated control-byte inputs; 200 repetitions per shape/context mode. Process CPU includes compressor allocation/free only when reuse is off. Excludes Rust buffer initialization, framing, storage and SDK work.
